subject: Acme — post-demo follow-up: audit logs, PII controls, and evidence next steps
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: John Lutz <john.lutz@acme.com>, security-team@acme.com
Cc: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-22T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Acme — post-demo follow-up: audit logs, PII controls, and evidence next steps

Hi John / Acme security team,

Thanks for taking the demo this morning — appreciated the clear questions on data handling. Per our call, I wanted to summarize what we covered, answer the outstanding items, and propose concrete next steps so your compliance team can validate controls quickly.

Recap (high level):
- Scope: Redwood Hosted inference used by Acme — customer data (requests + optional context) ingested by the inference endpoint.
- PII discussion: default collection is request metadata + model input; we support masking/pseudonymization at ingestion and customer-configurable retention.
- Audit logging: API-level audit logs capture who (internal user/service account), what (endpoint, model, request id), when (UTC timestamp), and action (create/read/export).

Outstanding questions we flagged:
1) Exact fields included in the audit export (schema).
2) Export formats (CSV/JSONL) and examples.
3) Retention window and ability to set custom retention for Acme.
4) Proof of access: how to demonstrate who viewed/exported logs (evidence artifacts).
5) Data residency options for logs and request payloads.

Quick answers (short):
- Schema: audit exports include event_id, timestamp_utc, actor_id (internal user or service principal), actor_type (user/service), remote_ip, request_id, model, route, action, resource_id, changes_summary, and optional user_id_hash (if pseudonymization enabled).
- Formats: UI export supports CSV; API /exports endpoints return JSONL and compressed tar.gz with CSV.
- Retention: default 13 months on Hosted; Dedicated/Private customers can configure shorter/longer via retention policy (policy applies to both logs and raw request payloads).
- Access proof: we store export events as separate immutable audit objects (export_event) with signer, timestamp, and signed URL evidence; those are included when we produce compliance packs.
- Residency: logs can be stored in the region of the customer (US / EU) for Dedicated/Private. Hosted supports regional tenancy in major cloud regions.

Attachments: I attached a short audit playbook (redwood_audit_playbook_v1.pdf) and a small synthetic sample export (sample_audit_export_20260322.csv) to show the schema and typical rows.

Proposed next steps (mutual action plan):
- I will: send the sample export and audit playbook (attached) by EOD today; provide the API export endpoint details and a small script to produce CSV/JSONL exports.
- Acme: confirm which artifacts you need for your evidentiary review (sample export + mapping, signed export event, or full compliance pack).
- Schedule: if helpful, let's meet Tues 24 Mar 14:00 PT for a short walkthrough of the export and to validate the mapping.

If you want, we can also produce a one-off compliance bundle with: sample export, export_event evidence, and access logs covering the last 30 days. That typically takes 2–3 business days to compile for Hosted customers.

Thanks —
Sean
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0182

From: John Lutz <john.lutz@acme.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: security-team@acme.com
Date: 2026-03-22T17:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Acme — post-demo follow-up: audit logs, PII controls, and evidence next steps

Sean — thanks for the thorough recap. A couple clarifications so we can scope the evidence request: 

1) For actor_id: will that be an email address or internal service principal id? Our auditors will want to map actor_id to our SSO identities.
2) For user_id_hash: is the hashing deterministic so our downstream systems can join without exposing raw PII? Also, can you provide the hashing algorithm and salt management?
3) Retention: is the 13 months SLA fixed on Hosted? We may request 18 months for a subset of logs — is that possible?
4) Export format: CSV is fine but we prefer JSONL for structured fields (changes_summary). Can the API deliver a daily archive for a given date range via an endpoint?

Finally, one ask from our security lead: can you provide an example of the "export_event" evidence object you mentioned — we need to see the fields that prove who triggered an export and when (and the signed URL metadata). If you can send a sample export_event and a small sample audit export, that will let us evaluate quickly.

Happy to meet Tues if you think a live walkthrough is useful. Thanks,
John
Director, Security Engineering | Acme Corp

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: John Lutz <john.lutz@acme.com>, security-team@acme.com
Cc: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-23T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Acme — post-demo follow-up: audit logs, PII controls, and evidence next steps

On Mon, Mar 22, 2026 at 5:03 PM John Lutz <john.lutz@acme.com> wrote:
> Sean — thanks for the thorough recap. A couple clarifications so we can scope the evidence request:
> 1) For actor_id: will that be an email address or internal service principal id? Our auditors will want to map actor_id to our SSO identities.

Good questions — answers below: 
- actor_id: the audit field "actor_id" is the internal unique identifier used by Redwood (service principals and internal users). For user-facing events (console actions) we also include actor_email when available; you can map actor_id <-> actor_email to your SSO mapping. For SSO-initiated events we capture the external SAML/SCIM id in actor_external_id.

- user_id_hash: yes, deterministic hashing is supported. We use HMAC-SHA256 with a customer-provided salt when you opt-in (customer-owned salt recommended for maximum assurance). We'll include the algorithm and a short note in the playbook. With deterministic HMAC you can join across exports without revealing raw PII.

- Retention: default Hosted tier is 13 months; we can request 18 months as an exception for your account and present it as a custom retention policy to engineering — this is feasible but requires a contract addendum for Hosted. Dedicated/Private customers can set retention directly via policy config.

- Export API: yes — the /v1/audit/exports endpoint supports a date-range query and returns a signed object that references a JSONL or CSV archive (gzip). We can schedule a one-off daily archive for a specific date range and generate a download link.

Sample export_event (example row):
export_event_id: ee_20260322_0001
triggered_by: sean_gallagher (internal user id: u_9273)
triggered_by_email: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
triggered_at_utc: 2026-03-22T14:58:23Z
export_format: csv
export_range_start: 2026-02-22T00:00:00Z
export_range_end: 2026-03-22T00:00:00Z
signed_url: https://s3.amazonaws.com/redwood-exports/ee_20260322_0001.csv?signature=XXXXXXXX
signature_meta: {algorithm=RSA-SHA256, signer=redwood-export-service, key_id=k_88}

I attached a tiny synthetic CSV (sample_audit_export_20260322.csv) showing five example rows and the header mapping. The playbook includes the full schema and a short FAQ on how we map SSO IDs.

Next steps:
- I'll assemble the one-off compliance bundle (sample export + export_event + short mapping doc) and deliver it by EOB Monday (2026-03-23). That should be sufficient for your initial audit review.
- If your auditors want signed export bundles spanning a longer range, we can produce that within 2–3 business days after scope is confirmed.

Ava — adding you to confirm we can deliver the export_event sample and the bundle by EOB Monday.

Thanks,
Sean

From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-03-23T10:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Acme — post-demo follow-up: audit logs, PII controls, and evidence next steps

John / Sean — noted. I will coordinate the compliance bundle (we'll include: sample_audit_export_20260322.csv, a redacted export_event.json snippet, and a short mapping table). Also will pull the SOC 2 artifact pack that references log collection & retention for your auditors.

Proposed meeting: Tue 2026-03-24 14:00 PT (30 minutes) — demo of the export flow + Q&A. I can invite our Solutions Engineer to walk the API call.

A few operational notes:
- Export bundles for Hosted accounts are compiled by our Compliance team and stored in an encrypted bucket; we provide a signed URL and include signer metadata.
- For HMAC salts: we recommend customer-provided salt for deterministic pseudonymization; if customer opts not to supply a salt we can still pseudonymize but cannot guarantee cross-export joins.

I'll post the calendar invite if that time works.

Thanks,
Ava
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: John Lutz <john.lutz@acme.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-24T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Acme — post-demo follow-up: audit logs, PII controls, and evidence next steps

Thanks — Tue 14:00 PT works for us. Please include the sample export and the export_event sample in the calendar materials so our auditors can triage before the call. We specifically want to confirm: 1) actor_external_id mapping for SSO events, 2) the presence of remote_ip for API calls, and 3) the signing metadata on export_event.

If you can also include a short note on how long signed URLs remain valid (we prefer short-lived URLs with an audit record), that will help.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.
John
